author: Not Specified
description: Minerva Humanoids, a robotics company developing semi-autonomous humanoid robots for dangerous tasks in energy and public safety sectors, has completed a $10M pre-seed funding round led by General Catalyst. description: Minerva Humanoids, a robotics startup founded by former MIT CSAIL and Tesla researchers, has raised $10 million in pre-seed funding led by General Catalyst to develop Roger, a semi-autonomous humanoid robot designed for hazardous missions in energy and public safety sectors. The robot enables remote operators to perform dangerous tasks like offshore oil operations and explosive device disposal while remaining physically safe, with the company launching commercial pilot projects in fall 2026.

title: Here's Why SpaceX's AI Infrastructure in Space "Moonshot" Won't Uproot Neocloud Companies
author: Marc Guberti
description: SpaceX launched a test satellite with Google's TPUs to explore orbital data centers, but satellite-based data centers will cost 2.5-3x more than Earth-based facilities. Tech giants need computing power immediately and are investing heavily in neocloud companies like Nebius and Iren, which have available megawatt capacity and scaling pipelines. Orbital data centers are unlikely to replace terrestrial data centers in the near term.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While SpaceX achieved a milestone launching Google's TPUs, the article emphasizes significant cost barriers (2.5-3x more expensive) and Elon Musk's history of missing ambitious timelines. The technology is promising but faces substantial hurdles before commercial viability.

Alphabet is actively testing orbital data center technology through Project Suncatcher, showing innovation leadership. However, the article suggests this is a long-term bet while immediate compute needs are being met through terrestrial solutions.

title: Stellantis N.V. vs. Tesla: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Pamela Kock
description: The article compares Stellantis and Tesla as investment options in 2026. Stellantis, a legacy automaker with 14 brands, trades at a lower valuation but reported a €22.3 billion net loss in FY 2025 with negative free cash flow. Tesla remains profitable with $3.8 billion net income and $6.2 billion free cash flow despite slower EV market growth, positioning it as the more attractive investment despite its higher valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company reported a substantial €22.3 billion net loss in FY 2025, negative industrial free cash flow of €4.5 billion, negative gross margin of -168%, and a challenging turnaround strategy with uncertain execution despite lower valuation metrics.

Company maintained profitability with $3.8 billion net income despite cooling EV market, generated $6.2 billion in free cash flow, maintains minimal debt (0.1x debt-to-equity), and has growth opportunities in energy storage and autonomous vehicles.

title: 5 Key AI Investment News Items
author: Na
description: AMD reports sustained high demand for compute chips with plans to substantially increase supply by 2027. SpaceX and TSMC explore a Texas semiconductor partnership through the Terafab project to consolidate chip production. Anthropic commits $518 billion in non-cancelable cloud spending over the next decade. Zscaler warns that autonomous AI agents will become a major cybersecurity risk vector. Wells Fargo raises Meta's price target to $1,000 citing AI cycle expansion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: CEO Lisa Su confirmed demand exceeds supply with expectations for strong demand to continue for several years, and AMD plans to substantially increase supply in 2027.
SpaceX is advancing the Terafab project and exploring partnership with TSMC for Texas semiconductor facility, which would reduce technological risk and accelerate time-to-market for complex chips.
TSMC is positioned as potential anchor client for Terafab Texas facility, leveraging its leading-edge lithography expertise and strengthening its role in the AI infrastructure buildout.
Tesla is part of the Terafab initiative to consolidate semiconductor production and reduce supply chain dependency, supporting its compute demands.
Zscaler reaffirmed guidance and highlighted robust cybersecurity demand driven by the rise of autonomous AI agents, positioning the company to benefit from emerging security threats.
Wells Fargo raised Meta's price target to $1,000 and maintains overweight rating, citing Muse driving a larger long-term AI cycle expansion.
